metrics.label: Brent crude
metrics.blurb: The global benchmark price for crude oil. Most oil cargoes price off it.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote, then the daily oil report, then EIA/FRED

metrics.label: WTI crude
metrics.blurb: The US crude benchmark. Its gap to Brent drives US export volumes.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote, then the daily oil report, then EIA/FRED

metrics.label: Dutch TTF gas
metrics.blurb: Europe's benchmark gas price, set in the Netherlands.
metrics.fallback: read from the daily European gas report

metrics.label: Henry Hub gas
metrics.blurb: The US benchmark gas price, set in Louisiana.

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)
metrics.blurb: Price of coal delivered into northwest Europe. A dry bulk demand signal.
metrics.fallback: CNBC lists ICE API2 but returns it undated; nothing else free publishes it.
metrics.source: ICE API2 Rotterdam Coal via CNBC

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil
metrics.blurb: A refined product price that tracks what bunker fuel costs.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote (ULSD heating oil front-month)

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline
metrics.blurb: US gasoline price. Strong margins here pull product tankers west.

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding dry bulk freight futures. A rough daily read on bulker sentiment.
metrics.source: Breakwave Dry Bulk Shipping ETF via CNBC

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.
metrics.source: Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF via CNBC

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.
metrics.source: Baltic Exchange via Hellenic Shipping News

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

rates.label: VLCC (TD3C, AG→China)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 2m-barrel crude tanker on the Arabian Gulf to China run. The most quoted tanker rate in the world.

rates.label: Suezmax (TD20, W.Africa→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 1m-barrel crude tanker from West Africa to Europe.

rates.label: Aframax (TD7, N.Sea→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 600k-barrel crude tanker on a short North Sea haul — the route closest to Norwegian crude exports.

rates.label: LR2 (TC1, AG→Japan)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a large product tanker carrying clean refined products.

rates.label: MR (TC2, Rotterdam→NY)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a mid-size product tanker on the transatlantic gasoline run.

rates.label: MR (TC14, US Gulf→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a mid-size product tanker carrying clean products east across the Atlantic.

brief.text:
The clearest signal in today's data is on the oil side: Brent crude, the main international benchmark, is $96.17 a barrel, up $1.56 or 1.6% today, with WTI, its US equivalent, at $84.88, up $1.20 or 1.4%. Alongside that, Gibson is reported saying tanker day rates for Strait of Hormuz transits remain above $1 million — relevant because the only VLCC figure we hold, the TD3C Arabian Gulf–China trip, was 1,079,794 USD/day when observed on Sunday 22 November. A VLCC is a very large crude carrier, roughly two million barrels; TCE, or time charter equivalent, is the daily earnings a voyage delivers after voyage costs. No freight benchmark in this data has refreshed today, so treat all rate levels as background.

On prices, bunkers moved in different directions today and the data does not explain why: VLSFO, the 0.5% sulphur fuel most ships burn, is $809.50/t in Singapore, down $24.00 (-2.9%), while Houston is $720.00/t, up $12.00 (+1.7%), Rotterdam $676.00/t, up $2.50, and Fujairah $780.00/t, down $7.00. Gasoil is $3.73/gal, up 0.9%; gasoline is unchanged at $2.44/gal; Henry Hub gas is $3.63/mmBtu, down 0.7%. The diesel crack against Brent — the refining margin on diesel — stands at $60.70/bbl today, and the Brent–WTI spread at $11.29/bbl. On dry bulk, the Baltic Dry Index was 3,107 points on Wednesday 25 November, up 39 (+1.3%), with the Capesize index (largest bulkers, mainly iron ore and coal) at 5,014 and Panamax at 2,223 the same day. Coal API2 at $133.50/t did not refresh.

Running stories: the Saudi-Houthi strikes on Ras Tanura and Hodeidah had no new headline today and are unchanged. Hormuz attacks are unchanged on the security side, but the Gibson report today keeps the earnings impact live. Drone strikes on Russian-linked shipping and the Russian refining and diesel-export story both had no news today. MEPC85 still opens on 30 November with LNG carbon accounting unsettled. New today: the US announced fresh tariffs on China, the EU and a dozen other economies, with trade press flagging possible disruption to container shipping.

Watch two things: whether Baltic tanker and dry indices refresh tomorrow, since nothing has updated since 22–25 November; and tariff retaliation headlines, which bear directly on box trades.

storylines.title: New US tariffs on China, EU and others
storylines.what: The US announced plans for a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies, citing overcapacity, after the Supreme Court found earlier sweeping import taxes unconstitutional.
storylines.why_it_matters: Tariff rounds redirect and distort container trade flows and can disrupt box shipping volumes and routings.
storylines.latest: Tariffs announced today; trade press reports they could again disrupt and distort container shipping and trade.
sources: U.S. Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
Tariffs return to haunt box shipping

storylines.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue, following tanker incidents near Oman, a mine strike east of Hormuz and a projectile hit on an outbound tanker.
storylines.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and mines raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings, slow transits and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude, product and gas ton-miles.
storylines.latest: Gibson reported that tanker day rates for Hormuz transits remain above $1 million despite charter rates coming off historic highs.
sources: Gibson: Tanker Day Rates for Hormuz Transits Remain Above $1 Million

storylines.title: Saudi-Houthi strikes hit energy and port infrastructure
storylines.what: Riyadh, the Houthi-controlled port of Hodeidah and the Saudi terminal at Ras Tanura were hit in an exchange of fire earlier this week.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on a major crude loading terminal and a Red Sea port threaten liftings, raise war-risk premiums and can reroute crude and product tonnage away from the region.

storylines.title: Drone strikes on Russian-linked shipping beyond the Black Sea
storylines.what: The Russian RoRo Sparta II was struck by a suspected drone in the Baltic and drifted into Finnish waters, and Ukrainian drone boats attacked Russian warships at Benghazi in Libya.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes in the Baltic and Mediterranean extend the war-risk zone for merchant shipping far beyond the Black Sea, affecting insurance cover, routing and port calls.

storylines.title: Russian refining damage and diesel export limits
storylines.what: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October, on top of a Russian ban on most diesel exports extended to end-January.
storylines.why_it_matters: Lost Russian refining and export restrictions reshape clean product ton-miles, pulling diesel from longer-haul sources and changing MR and LR employment.

storylines.title: IMO net-zero rules for LNG and alternative fuels
storylines.what: The IMO's Marine Environment Protection Committee opens MEPC85 on 30 November without final rules on how LNG, bio-LNG and e-LNG carbon values are measured under the Net-Zero Framework.
storylines.why_it_matters: The accounting treatment of LNG determines the compliance economics of LNG-fuelled tonnage and newbuilding decisions, including LNG carrier and dual-fuel orders now being placed.
storylines.latest: No rules news today, but further alternative-fuel tonnage was reported: COSL ordered 46 LNG-powered PSVs in China, SeaRoad took delivery of an LNG-powered RoRo, and Hudong-Zhonghua set a Chinese record with 12 large LNG carriers delivered this year.
